title: Germany – Carpentry installation work – Dynamisches Beschaffungssystem für Tischlerarbeiten für diverse Liegenschaften in Berlin
description: Als öffentlicher Auftraggeber verwaltet die Berliner Immobilienmanagement GmbH über 5.000 Liegenschaften des Landes Berlin. Hierzu zählen Liegenschaften zugehörig u.a. zum Allgemeinen Bestand (z.B. Verwaltungsbauten), zu Flüchtlingsunterbringungen, Kulturgebäuden, Polizei- und Feuerwehreinrichtungen sowie Schulen und Justizgebäuden. Im Zuge dieser Verwaltungseigenschaft besteht regelmäßig der Beschaffungsbedarf hinsichtlich vielfältiger Bauleistungen aus dem Bereich der Tischlerarbeiten. Im Rahmen des dynamischen Beschaffungssystems sollen daher regelmäßig Ausschreibungen für Tischlerarbeiten in überwiegend Bestandsgebäuden durchführt werden. Ziel ist es, einen Bieterpool aufzubauen, der für zukünftige Ausschreibungen zur Verfügung steht. Die Aufnahme in den Bieterpool ermöglicht die Teilnahme an zukünftigen Ausschreibungen für Tischlerarbeiten. Unter anderem sollen Leistungen über die dynamische Beschaffung bzgl. folgender Bereiche abgedeckt werden: - Abbruch Bestandselemente - Entsorgung der abgebrochenen Bestandselemente gem. VwVBU - Zerstörungsarmer Rückbau Bestandselemente (für die Wiederverwendung) - Innentür- und Fensterelemente - Außentür- und Fensterelemente Holz - Außentür- und Fensterelemente Kunststoff - Tore/ Türblätter-Holzrahmen / Holzwerkstoffrahmen - Fensterbänke-Holz/ Holzwerkstoff - Fensterläden Holz - Holztreppen - Geländer - Holzleisten / Holzwerkstoffleisten - Sanitärtrennwände - Deckenbekleidung, Wandbekleidung, Einbaumöbel - Mobile Trennwandsysteme - Schutz von Bau- und Anlageteilen - Einbaumöbel, z.B. Einbauregale/Schränke, Tische - Wandvertäfelungen - Sonstige Leistungen. Es besteht die Möglichkeit, dass auch Arbeiten an denkmalgeschützten Gebäuden erforderlich sind. Bei bestimmten Aufträgen (insbesondere bzgl. Portfolio Polizei oder Justizgebäuden) kann eine Sicherheits- und /oder Zuverlässigkeitsüberprüfung des eingesetzten Personals erforderlich sein. Weitere Einzelheiten siehe Verfahrensbrief und Kurzerläuterung in den Vergabeunterlagen.

title: ROKS TP7 : Lot Turbine
description:
Dans le cadre du projet « ROKS-TP7 Centrale de dotation d'Ova Spin », l'installation de dotation, composée d'un groupe de machines comprenant une turbine, un générateur, une vanne sphérique, la conduite forcée et l'unité de contrôle commande datant de la mise en service initiale en 1968, va faire l'objet d'une révision complète après plus de 50 ans de fonctionnement.


L'objectif de cette révision complète de la turbine de dotation est de la mettre à niveau avec l'état actuel de la technique et de la remettre en parfait état mécanique.

La turbine de dotation a fait l’objet d’une révision partielle pour la dernière fois en 2002.


En résumé, les travaux principaux suivants sont prévus :

- Révision complète du générateur existant. Ce point ne fait pas partie de cet appel d’offres, mais fait l’objet d’un lot distinct

- Révision complète de la turbine avec renouvellement intégral de la protection anticorrosion

- Utilisation de la roue de rechange existante, des aubes directrices de rechange ainsi que d’autres pièces de rechange disponibles

- Enlèvement et élimination des peintures contenant des PCB

- Éventuellement, un nouvel échangeur de chaleur pour l'huile du palier de la turbine

- Remplacement de l’ancienne instrumentation


Caractéristiques techniques de la turbine de dotation :

Turbine Francis horizontale

Marque/type : Bell

Débit d'eau : 0,9 m³/s

Hauteur de chute : 57,64 m

Puissance : 500 kW

Mise en service : décembre 1968

Dernière révision : 2002

Vitesse de rotation : 750 tr/min

title: Désenfumage Check-in 3
description:
À l’aéroport de Zurich, les zones passagers situées dans la partie nord de l’Airport Shopping font l’objet d’un réaménagement et d’un agrandissement complets (projet ELP). Le concept de désenfumage ELP couvre les zones de l’Airport Shopping concernées par le projet ELP, y compris le secteur du Check-in 3, ainsi que certaines parties des parkings P1 et P2. Il constitue la base des mesures de désenfumage prévues dans le périmètre ELP.


En raison de l’augmentation de la surface de l’Airport Shopping, le système de désenfumage mécanique doit toutefois être étendu au-delà du périmètre ELP. Pour la zone du Check-in 3, il est prévu de doubler la capacité de désenfumage en termes de débit d’air extrait. En outre, un désenfumage mécanique supplémentaire devra être mis en place dans deux autres zones de moindre taille appartenant à des partenaires de l'aéroport.


La planification et la réalisation du système de désenfumage mécanique seront confiées à un planificateur général, couvrant l’ensemble des disciplines spécialisées faisant l’objet de l’appel d’offres. La direction générale du projet incombe à la gestion de la construction.


Le marché porte sur les prestations de mandataire général pour les phases SIA 31 à 53.

title: SPATZ Plastique renforcé de fibres de verre + peinture
description:
Dans le cadre de la remise en état à l'atelier de Meiringen, les surfaces en fibre de verre renforcée (FV) et peintes des 10 rames motrices doivent être rénovées. En février 2026, un état des lieux et un diagnostic ont été effectués sur le véhicule de référence SPATZ 130 009-04 (annexes D1 et D2). Les dommages suivants ont notamment été constatés

- jupes de toit fortement altérées par les intempéries et décolorées (blanc/gris)

- fissures et impacts sur les façades en PRV et les jupes avant

- corrosion accompagnée de cloques sur les cadres de fenêtres des voitures d'extrémité

- dommages à la peinture (impacts de pierres) ainsi que des traces de rayures dans le vernis transparent sur les caisses des voitures

- traces dues au vieillissement au niveau des joints d'étanchéité des vitres avant et à la jonction entre la voiture d'extrémité et la partie avant


Pour cette mission, le spécialiste doit posséder les compétences et l'expérience nécessaires afin de mener à bien ce projet avec le niveau de qualité requis. Compte tenu des exigences liées à l'exploitation ferroviaire, une grande vigilance en matière de délais, de coûts et d'environnement est requise.


  • Lot 1 : Rénovation en PRV et nouvelle peinture de 160 jupes de toit (16 pièces par rame automotrice) conformément à la spécification technique de peinture 114089 C, teintes RAL 7016 gris anthracite et RAL 9010 blanc pur, brillant
  • Lot 2 : Réparation des panneaux en PRV et nouvelle peinture des façades, rénovation des vitres et retouches de peinture des caisses (voiture d'extrémité 1, voiture centrale, voiture d'extrémité 2) sur 10 rames
  • Lot 2 : délai d'exécution d'environ 5 semaines par rame automotrice (2 semaines par voiture d'extrémité, 1 semaine par voiture centrale ; jusqu'à 2 semaines en cas de dommages dus à la corrosion sur la voiture centrale)
  • documentation complète comprenant les procès-verbaux de fabrication et de contrôle (épaisseur de couche, quadrillage, degré de brillance)

buyer: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board
title: Pre Front Door Integrated Urgent Care Services
description:
NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board (CW ICB) are seeking expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced providers for the provision of a comprehensive Pre-Front Door Integrated Urgent Care (IUC) model across Coventry and Warwickshire.

This model requires a single, accountable Lead Provider in each of the two geographical areas:
Coventry (Lot 1) and
Warwickshire (Lot 2)

The appointed Lead Providers will be responsible for the end-to-end design, mobilisation, delivery, clinical governance and continuous improvement of a whole-system urgent care pathway spanning NHS 111 interfaces, GP out of hours, UTC/MIU, ambulance conveyance alternatives, Emergency Department front-door streaming, same-day emergency care, diagnostics, community response and neighbourhood urgent care pathways.

The ICB is not seeking a provider of isolated urgent care components. It is seeking an organisation with the scale, capability, and system leadership to deliver an integrated Lead Provider model. Providers must therefore bring together all interdependent services, healthcare professionals and current Providers, including urgent primary care, community response, and mental health crisis interfaces, into a coherent, accountable and high-performing model.

Contract Length is expected to be 5 years, commencing 1st September 2027 with the Commissioner having the option to extend the Contract for up to a further 5 years.

Further details are provided in VI.3

title: Production of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) Lethality Payloads at Pine Bluff Arsenal
description: 30 OCT 2026 The response due date is 4:00 PM CST on 14 DEC 2026. Submit responses to this request for partnership solutions to debby.c.broyles.civ@army.mil and heather.b.johns.civ@army.mil with subject line: PSO Response Production of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) Lethality Payloads at Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA). Partnership Solutions Opening � Request for Whitepapers Agency: Department of War (DoW) / Army Materiel Command (AMC) Notice Type: Partnership Solutions Opening (PSO) Title: Production of sUAS Lethality Payloads at PBA. 1.0 INTRODUCTION & AUTHORITY The U.S. Army Materiel Command (AMC) is issuing this request for partnership solutions via white paper submission solely for market research, planning, and concept exploration regarding a potential Public-Private Partnership (P3) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 7544. The Government is requesting specific conceptual solutions on how to optimally structure and execute P3 Cooperative Arrangements. The core objective is to leverage private investment to modernize Government facilities to Industry 4.0 and 5.0 automation standards. Industry 4.0 is defined as the Fourth Industrial Revolution, is characterized by the "Smart Factory." It aims to create highly efficient, autonomous production lines by integrating cyber-physical systems with the Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud computing. Industry 5.0 is not meant to replace Industry 4.0 but to refine it. It recognizes that pure automation can overlook human creativity and environmental impact. It places the well-being of the worker and the planet at the center of the industrial process. This modernization will enable authorized co-production and facility-use activities that mutually benefit the Government's national security mission and the private partner's commercial enterprise. Disclaimer: This PSO does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), nor is it a procurement action governed by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). The Government is not obligated to enter into any cooperative arrangement or agreement because of this PSO and will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submitting a response. 2.0 PROBLEM STATEMENT PBA is requesting a commercial partnership to support the development and production of lethal energetic payloads for sUAS and Electronic Safe & Arming Devices (ESAD). These efforts include scaling low-cost, modernized sUAS lethality and energetic payload manufacturing. PBA intends for flexible production lines with ability to accommodate modular manufacturing capabilities for differing explosives, varying payload sizes, explosive safe and arming devices, energetic airframes, etc. PBA can provide both logistical and facility support, including approximately 100,000 square feet of storage and production capacity. The government has various 1 or 2 story buildings available in area 34-000 ranging in size from 396 sq ft to 13,551 sq ft with various existing capabilities to include electricity, water, air sewer, Natural Gas, and/or steam. Additional building details provided in Attachment 1. The production facilities were constructed in 1941-42 for the war effort to handle highly volatile chemical, pyrotechnic, and incendiary compounds. Structurally and architecturally, these buildings reflect a combination of standardized strict hazard segmentation, and fortified safety engineering. Buildings are constructed with heavy, reinforced concrete interior blast walls and thick foundations, but with deliberately weak, lightweight exterior walls and roofs. PBA can provide the following support: � Direct labor � Engineering � Base operations � Logistical support � Environmental and safety support, including leveraging PBA's existing Explosive Site Safety Plans to expedite the mandatory joint site-licensing updates required for the partner's specific energetic footprint and, as applicable, for any non-Department of Defense owned toxic or hazardous materials, supporting Government coordination and processing of a 10 U.S.C. 2692 exception request; the contractor remains responsible for providing the technical, environmental, safety, and operational information required to support that request. � Utilities: Existing utility systems vary by facility as shown in Attachment 1. The contractor is responsible for any necessary capital investments required to utilize these utilities, including the procurement and installation of utility meters, sub-meters, service hookups, and distribution lines. 3.0 FINANCIAL & INVESTMENT REQUIREMENTS (CAPITAL EXPENDITURES) To accelerate modernization without requiring upfront Government funding, the selected industry partner(s) must meet the following financial parameters: Private Equity Financed Capital Expenditures (CapEx): An industry partner(s) must utilize private equity or internal corporate capital to fund 100% of the modernization CapEx for the targeted building(s). Scope of CapEx: This investment must cover all necessary facility upgrades, structural modifications, equipment procurement, software integration, and physical installation. Permanent upgrades become Government property upon installation, with the contractor retaining operational use for the duration of the agreement. 4.0 OPERATIONAL CONCEPT: COOPERATIVE ARRANGEMENT In exchange for the capital investment, the Government will enter a Cooperative Arrangement pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 7544(a). Commercial Capacity Guarantee (Facilities Use): In accordance with 10 U.S.C 7544(b)(5), an industry partner will be granted a facilities-use contract guaranteeing a portion of the capacity of the modernized/new lines for their own commercial requirements, with the precise amount to be negotiated based on the overall structure of the partnership, other in-kind considerations offered, etc. Excess Capacity Utilization: Pursuant to 10 U.S.C 7544(c)(3), an industry partner is authorized to use any additional excess capacity not actively utilized or identified for future by the Government. Non-Interference Mandate: As required by 10 U.S.C 7544(c)(2), all commercial production must not interfere with the performance of work for the Department of War. Build-to-Operate (BTO) Model: To accelerate modernization, the cooperative arrangement may utilize a BTO framework. The industry partner will develop, locate, and temporarily operate innovative technological capabilities at OIB sites until they recover their initial capital investment and realize an agreed upon profit. Upon reaching this threshold, operational control transitions to the OIB for long term sustainment, allowing the contractor to refocus on next generation innovation. This BTO model benefits the enterprise by optimizing both sectors' strengths and yields faster capability deployment during the innovation phase and steadier, modernized sustainment production within the OIB. 5.0 MANDATORY STATUTORY PROVISIONS (10 U.S.C. 7544) Indemnification: A selected Industry partner will be required to agree to the indemnity restrictions located at 10 U.S.C. 7544(c)(4). title: NIH MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES
description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES Solicitation No. 75N99027R00002 The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Acquisition and Logistics Management (OALM), Construction, A&E, Facilities and Leasing Office (CAFLO), anticipates issuing a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a Multiple-Award Construction Contract (MACC) to support the ongoing construction, alteration, repair, and maintenance requirements of the NIH Office of Research Facilities (ORF). The resulting contracts will be multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) construction contracts. Work will be authorized through individually issued task orders. This acquisition is anticipated to be conducted using competitive negotiated procedures under FAR Part 15. The Government intends to award multiple IDIQ construction contracts under FAR Subpart 16.5. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis. The anticipated aggregate ceiling is $3 billion over an eight-year ordering period. Individual construction requirements will be competed through task orders among eligible MACC awardees in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the resulting contracts. The solicitation and resulting contracts will include procedures for adding and removing awardees during that period (on/off ramp). The initial seed-project scope estimated construction magnitude, applicable evaluation factors, and proposal submission requirements will be provided in the solicitation. SCOPE OF WORK Work under the MACC will primarily consist of general construction and may include, but is not limited to, maintenance, repair, painting, alterations, architectural work, mechanical systems, electrical systems, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), civil work, earthwork, fencing, structural work, steel fabrication and welding, roofing, building renovations, demolition, new building construction, sustainable construction, design-bid-build, and design-build projects. Individual task orders may include one or more construction disciplines and will vary in size, scope, and complexity. All work will be performed in accordance with the requirements, specifications, drawings, and other documents applicable to each individual task order. LOCATIONS OF WORK The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Research Facilities (ORF) is the steward of NIH facilities and is responsible for the planning, design, construction, acquisition, maintenance and operation of NIH owned facilities, which include campuses in: � Bethesda, Maryland, � Frederick, Maryland, � Poolesville, Maryland, � Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, � The Rocky Mountain Laboratories (RML) in Hamilton, Montana. NAICS CODE AND SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. PSC Code: Y1JZ The corresponding small business size standard is $45 million. The NAICS code and small business size standard applicable to the initial seed project is also anticipated to be NAICS 236220 and $45 million, respectively. ACQUISITION STRATEGY AND ANTICIPATED AWARDS This acquisition will be conducted using full and open competition with reserves for eligible small business concerns. NIH anticipates awarding up to twenty (20) IDIQ contracts, consisting of: Approximately four (4) unrestricted/full-and-open awards; and Approximately sixteen (16) awards under small business reserves. The small business reserves are anticipated to include eligible concerns in the following categories: Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Small Business; Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); and Participants in the SBA 8(a) Business Development Program. The solicitation will identify the anticipated distribution of the sixteen (16) reserve awards among the applicable small business and socioeconomic categories and will establish the eligibility requirements applicable to each reserve. NIH anticipates approximately four (4) awards in each socioeconomic reserve. Offerors must meet all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the category under which they submit an offer. BONDING CAPACITY Offerors competing for an unrestricted/full-and-open award shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $100 million for a single project; and $300 million aggregate bonding capacity. Offerors competing for an award under a small business reserve shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $3 million for a single project; and $10 million aggregate bonding capacity. The solicitation will establish the specific documentation required to demonstrate bonding capacity. Performance and payment bond requirements applicable to individual construction task orders will be established in accordance with the solicitation, resulting contracts, applicable law and regulation, and the requirements of each task order. SMALL BUSINESS ELIGIBILITY AND JOINT VENTURES Offerors seeking an award under a small business reserve must satisfy all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the applicable reserve category and NAICS code. The solicitation will identify any documentation required to establish an offeror's eligibility for the applicable small business or socioeconomic category. Small business concerns intending to submit an offer as a joint venture must comply with all applicable SBA joint venture requirements, including applicable requirements governing SBA-approved Mentor-Prot�g� relationships. Prospective offerors should consult current SBA regulations and guidance concerning joint ventures and the SBA Mentor-Prot�g� Program at www.sba.gov. CONTRACT CEILING AND ORDERING PERIOD The aggregate maximum value of all contracts and task orders awarded under the MACC will not exceed $3,000,000,000.00 over the entire ordering period. The $3 billion ceiling applies collectively to all MACC contracts and is not a per-contractor ceiling. The anticipated ordering period will consist of one eight-year ordering period. There is no anticipated annual or individual-contractor ceiling other than limitations established by the terms of the resulting contracts and individual task orders. MACC holders will remain eligible to compete for task orders, subject to the terms and conditions of their contracts, until expiration of the ordering period or exhaustion of the aggregate MACC ceiling, whichever occurs first. TASK ORDERS All work under the MACC will be authorized through individual task orders. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis and will be separately priced. Each task order will establish the applicable scope of work, specifications and drawings, period of performance, applicable wage determination, bonding requirements, and other project-specific requirements. Task orders may be competed among all eligible MACC holders or restricted to eligible small business MACC holders in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated maximum value of an individual task order is $800 million. Eligibility to compete for individual task orders may be subject to project-specific requirements, including required bonding capacity. GUARANTEED MINIMUM The Government's guaranteed minimum under each resulting IDIQ contract will be $1,000. The guaranteed minimum will be satisfied through issuance of a task order. The $1,000 guaranteed minimum is a contractual minimum obligation and should not be interpreted as establishing the minimum dollar value of all future task orders. description: En el marco de las competencias que tiene atribuidas Turespaña ha obtenido la autorización del Consejo de Ministros para licitar la concesión de obra pública del Palacio de congresos de Madrid, en la reunión celebrada el 6 de mayo de 2025. El complejo va a ser objeto de una rehabilitación integral que comenzó ya en 2023 con la obra de remodelación y ampliación del Edificio B para convertirse en la futura sede de Onu-Turismo. La nueva licitación tiene por objeto la concesión de obra pública del resto de inmuebles que integran el complejo. El adjudicatario se encargará de redactar el proyecto de ejecución, realizar las obras y explotar el Palacio de Congresos y su aparcamiento por un plazo de concesión de 40 años a cambio de un canon anual que abonará a Turespaña. El plazo de la concesión es de 40 años, incluyendo una fase de redacción de proyecto de ejecución y obra de 48 meses. El CAPEX es de 105,7 Millones de euros, y la TIR de proyecto de 7,65%. Una vez completados todos los trámites administrativos, Turespaña publicará la licitación en la Plataforma de Contratación del Sector Público y el Diario Oficial de la Unión Europa (DOUE). Los interesados en la licitación pueden consultar la documentación relativa al estudio de viabilidad y anteproyecto y proyecto básico en el Portal de Transparencia de Turespaña.

Autobusy, o których mowa w pkt 1 muszą: 1) spełniać wymagania techniczne określone w załączniku nr 3 do SWZ -OPZ; 2) być fabrycznie nowe, wg definicji z ustawy Prawo o ruchu drogowym z dnia 20 czerwca 1997 r., niskopodłogowe oraz posiadać aktualne świadectwo homologacji typu pojazdu WE wydane zgodnie z ustawą z dnia 14 kwietnia 2023 r. o systemach homologacji pojazdów oraz ich wyposażenia, odpowiadać parametrom techniczno-eksploatacyjnym określonym w obowiązujących przepisach określonych w Rozporządzeniu Ministra Infrastruktury w sprawie warunków technicznych pojazdów oraz zakresu ich niezbędnego wyposażenia; 3) być wyprodukowane nie wcześniej niż jeden rok przed dostawą, nieeksploatowane i nieużywane do badań, testów, prezentacji lub celów o podobnym charakterze; 4) być jednej marki, identyczne pod względem konstrukcyjnym, kompletacji, wyposażenia i kolorystyki (uzgodnionej z Zamawiającym zgodnie z Załącznikiem nr 3 do SWZ), oklejone logotypami Programu Fundusze Europejskie na Infrastrukturę, Klimat, Środowisko 2021-2027 (FEnIKS) (w uzgodnieniu z Zamawiającym). UWAGA: Przedmiot zamówienia musi być zgodny z zasadą DNSH („Do No Significant Harm” – nie czyń znaczącej szkody). o której mowa w rozporządzeniu (UE) 2020/852. Wykonawca zobowiązany jest do stosowania rozwiązań technicznych, technologicznych i organizacyjnych, które nie powodują znaczącej szkody dla celów środowiskowych,w szczególności w zakresie: łagodzenia zmian klimatu, adaptacji do zmian klimatu, odpowiedniego użytkowania i ochrony zasobów wodnych i morskich, ochrony środowiska gruntowo-wodnego, gospodarki o obiegu zamkniętym, w tym zapobieganiu powstawaniu odpadów i recyklingu, zapobiegania i kontroli zanieczyszczeniom powietrza, wody lub ziemi oraz ochrony i odbudowy bioróżnorodności i ekosystemów. Zastosowane materiały, urządzenia i technologie powinny charakteryzować się racjonalnym wykorzystaniem zasobów, ograniczeniem emisji i odpadów oraz trwałością w całym cyklu życia obiektu. Wykonawca udzieli Zamawiającemu pisemnej gwarancji na okres nie krótszy niż: 1) całopojazdowa – minimum 24 miesiące od daty odbioru końcowego, 2) na perforację spowodowaną korozją poszyć zewnętrznych oraz szkieletu nadwozia i podwozia jak również pęknięć konstrukcji szkieletu – minimum 120 miesięcy od daty odbioru końcowego, 3) na powłoki lakiernicze oraz antykorozyjne zabezpieczenie podwozia – minimum 60 miesiące od daty odbioru końcowego, 4) na magazyny energii elektrycznej - gwarancja trwałości i poprawnej pracy – minimum 120 miesięcy od daty odbioru końcowego.

title: Z1DA--FY27 Danville Mechanical MATOC SEED PROJECT NO: 550-26-106, Replace Air Handling Unit B58 at the VA Illiana Health Care System (VIHCS), Danville IL.
description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 3 of 4 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 4 DESCRIPTION PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The VA Illiana Health Care System (VIHCS), Danville IL, 1900 E Main St. Danville, IL 61832, has a need for a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for mechanical construction. The VA intends to award a MATOC for mechanical maintenance, repair, alteration, and repair of buildings and other real property belonging to this facility, with task orders ranging in value from $2,000 to $3,000,000. The maximum net value of all task orders and modifications, combined for all contractors issued under this MATOC shall not exceed $20 Million. The net aggregate value for the individualized contractor for all task orders and modifications issued against the MATOC shall not exceed $19 Million. The MATOC will include a five (5) year ordering period from date of award. The VA anticipates a minimum of two (2) IDIQ contract awards and shall reserve the right to make additional IDIQ awards. The primary purpose/work to be ordered under this contract is mechanical construction (NAICS 238220) but may include work incidental to the overall construction work, such as carpentry; asphalt and concrete paving; roofing; excavation; interior renovation; carpet, window, door installation; mechanical; electrical; plumbing; painting and stucco; demolition; masonry; fire protection; telecommunications; HVAC; and other construction-related work. As project requirements are defined, individual task order solicitations will be competitively issued to all selected MATOC contractors. The NAICS code for this procurement is 238220 with a size standard of $19.0 Million Dollars. The construction range for the seed project is between $1,000,000 and $2,000,000. Contractors will be required under the contract to have a minimum individual task order bonding capacity of $2,000,000 for the life of the contract. This acquisition shall be 100% set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SBVOSB) concerns per the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127 (Public Law 109-461). In accordance with VAAR 819.7003(b), at the time of submission of proposal, the offeror must represent that is a SDVOSB concern, a small business concern under the NAICS code assigned to the acquisition, and has a SBA SDVOSB Certification Veteran Small Business Certification (www.sba.gov). This Pre-Solicitation notice is NOT a request for proposals or submittals of any kind. The VA plans to issue the official solicitation 36C25227R0002 on or about 11/20/2026. The solicitation will be posted to https://www.SAM.gov.

title: E60HN-21HDMS High Density Mobile Shelving - HDMS RFSA
description: On-going opportunity for qualification for supply arrangement series E60HN-21HDMS the Supply Arrangement for the relocation, modifications, extensions and consultation services to existing high density mobile shelving (HDMS) as well as installation of new HDMS systems. This RFSA is for deliveries in all regions of Canada, excluding Nunavut and locations that are subject to Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements (CLCAs). The RFSA will simultaneously include a provision to establish a duplicate Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Businesses (PSIB). title: Acquisition d'un camion-citerne feux de forêts moyen
description:
L’objet du marché consiste en une offre d’une validité de 9 mois pour l’acquisition d’un camion-citerne feux de forêts moyen (CCFM, selon la norme NF S 61-518).

Le véhicule aura pour tâche d’intervenir dans des milieux tout-terrains (forestiers) et non carrossés afin de lutter contre les incendies de forêts ainsi que sur des feux d’espaces naturels et des inondations et crues.

Le véhicule est susceptible d'être ravitaillé en eau naturelle, chargée en particules sablonneuses ou terreuses et présentant des caractéristiques d'acidité prononcées. La fabrication du véhicule et de son équipement doit être garantie afin d’assurer, entre autres, l'étanchéité des cuves et le fonctionnement efficace du dispositif d'autoprotection thermique dans les conditions décrites ci-dessus.

Le véhicule doit répondre aux spécifications techniques (éliminatoires) suivantes :

  • Fournir un véhicule de type CCFM conforme à la norme NF S 61-518 (catégorie 3, classe M).
  • La hauteur hors tout est de maximum 3'300 mm selon la norme NF S 61-518.
  • Le véhicule possède 2 essieux.
  • Le poids total du véhicule est de minimum 7'500 kg et maximum 16'000 kg selon la norme NF S 61-518.
  • Le véhicule est équipé d’une cabine double possédant 4 places assises dans le sens de marche.
  • Le circuit de commande de la prise de mouvement et les organes associés à la pompe doivent résister à une température de minimum 130°C durant minimum 10 minutes. Si ces circuits ou organes ne satisfont pas aux prescriptions ci-dessus, ils doivent être protégés (selon la norme NF S 61-518).
  • Les organes vulnérables ci-dessous doivent résister à une température de minimum 130°C durant minimum 10 minutes. Si ces circuits ou organes ne satisfont pas aux prescriptions, ils doivent être protégés (selon la norme NF S 61-518).

- Circuits de freinage et réservoirs de liquide de freins ;

- Circuit de diesel (du réservoir aux injecteurs) ;

- Circuits du dispositif d’autoprotection à l’exception de la commande extérieure ;

- Circuits électriques indispensables à la mobilité du véhicule ;

- Circuit de servitude pour prise de mouvement ;

- Batteries et leur support et/ou coffre ;

- Prise(s) d’air du moteur de l’engin, ses tubulures et ses composants.

  • Fournir une motorisation diesel (selon la norme NF S 61-518).
  • La prise d’air du moteur est située à un niveau supérieur à celui le plus haut de la motorisation (selon la norme NF S 61-518).
  • La profondeur du gué franchissable est de minimum 700 mm (selon la norme NF S 61-518).
  • Fournir une transmission 4x4 permanente.
  • Fournir une boîte de vitesses automatique, robotisée, sans pédale d’embrayage.
  • Le véhicule est équipé d’un frein de pente selon la norme NF S 61-510.
  • Fournir un système permettant de se déplacer à une vitesse comprise entre 3 et 10 km/h avec la prise de force enclenchée (Pump & roll).
  • Le véhicule est équipé de roues simples (pas de roues jumelées).
  • Le véhicule est équipé d’un tableau de commande situé à l’arrière.
  • Les citernes d’extinction et d’autoprotection sont en acier inoxydable.
  • La capacité de la citerne d’extinction est de minimum 3'000 litres.
  • La citerne d’extinction est équipée d’un trou d’homme.
  • La capacité de la citerne d’autoprotection est de 500 litres.
  • La citerne d’autoprotection est équipée d’un orifice d’inspection de minimum 150 mm de diamètre.
  • Fournir un réservoir de produit mouillant d’une capacité de minimum 60 litres, selon la norme NF S 61-518.
  • Le débit de l’ensemble du dispositif d’autoprotection est de minimum 60 l/min, selon la norme NF S 61-518.
  • Toutes les buses du dispositif d’autoprotection sont alimentées dans un délai de 20 secondes après l’activation du dispositif, selon la norme NF S 61-518.
  • L’autoprotection est efficace (selon la norme NF S 61-518) en maximum 60 secondes et doit toujours être efficace après 240 secondes.
  • Fournir une pompe à eau principale FPN 10-2000 conforme à la norme EN1028.
  • La pompe à eau principale est en bronze.
  • La citerne doit pouvoir être remplie par la pompe à eau principale en mode "Aspiration".
  • L’énergie nécessaire au dispositif d’alimentation de secours n’est pas fournie par un moteur thermique, selon la norme NF S 61-518.
  • Le dispositif d’alimentation de secours fonctionne pendant un minimum de 300 secondes, selon la norme NF S 61-518.
  • L’avant du véhicule est équipé d’un treuil d’autohalage possédant la force minimale selon la formule « Ft » de la norme NF S 61-518.
  • La cabine est équipée d’un système d’air respirable conforme aux normes NF S 61-518, NF EN 402 et NF EN 140.
  • L’autonomie du dispositif d’air respirable est de minimum 10 minutes avec 5 personnes consommant chacune 30 l/min, selon la norme NF S 61-518.
  • Le véhicule sera immatriculé en plaques bleues.
  • Le véhicule respectera les normes antipollution en vigueur au moment de la livraison.
  • Le véhicule est adapté au climat du Canton de Neuchâtel ainsi qu’au bâtiment où il sera stocké.
  • Les spécifications techniques avec la mention « éliminatoire » dans l’Annexe C sont toutes acceptées.

title: Muutosturvakoulutusten pienhankintarekisteri, uusi ilmoitus
description: Muutosturvakoulutusten pienhankintarekisteri, uusi ilmoitus Business Oulu -liikelaitos (jäljempänä myös "BusinessOulu", "Tilaaja" ja "Hankintayksikkö") pyytää tarjouksia Oulun seudun työllisyysalueella järjestettävistä muutosturvakoulutuksista (jäljempänä myös "muutosturva55+ -koulutus") tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Oulun seudun työllisyysalueeseen kuuluvat seuraavat kunnat Hailuoto, Ii, Kempele, Liminka, Lumijoki, Muhos, Oulu, Pudasjärvi, Tyrnävä, Utajärvi ja Vaala. Business Oulu -liikelaitoksen työllisyysjaosto on Oulun kaupungin organisaatioon kuuluva toimielin, joka vastaa työvoimapalvelujen järjestämisestä Oulun seudun työllisyysalueella. Hankinnalla perustetaan dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän toimintamalliin pohjautuva pienhankintarekisteri, johon hyväksytään kaikki tarjouspyynnön soveltuvuusvaatimukset ja tarjouspyynnössä esitetyt muut kriteerit täyttävät tarjoajat. Muutosturvakoulutuksella tuetaan työstään tuotannollisella tai taloudellisella perusteella irtisanottujen 55 vuotta täyttäneiden henkilöiden nopeaa uudelleen työllistymistä parantamalla heidän ammatillista osaamistaan tai yrittäjävalmiuksiaan. Muutosturvakoulutuksia säädellään julkisesta työvoima- ja yrityspalvelusta annetun lain 5a luvussa (916/2012). Pienhankintarekisteristä voidaan hankkia palveluita suoraan rekisteriin hyväksytyltä toimijalta tai kilpailuttamalla nopeutetulla aikataululla joko rajoitetulla menettelyllä tai kaikilta rekisteriin hyväksytyiltä tarjoajilta Hankinnasta kiinnostuneita ehdokkaita pyydetään jättämään osallistumishakemus Tarjouspalvelu.fi-portaalissa tämän osallistumispyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Hankinnasta julkaistaan tämä uusi ilmoitus teknisen virheen vuoksi. Edellinen ilmoitus avattiin hankintailmoitus 11.3.2025 ja siihen hyväksymispäätöksen (§49/2025, toimitettu 16.4.2025) saaneiden tarjoajien ei tarvitse jättää uutta osallistumisilmoitusta,

These services can include: Weed Control: This involves the removal and prevention of unwanted plants and weeds that can affect the health of desired plants and the aesthetics of the landscape. Services may include manual removal, chemical treatments, and organic solutions tailored to the specific needs of the area. Lawn Care: Regular mowing, edging, aeration, fertilization, and reseeding are part of lawn care services to ensure a lush and healthy lawn. Landscaping: Design and maintenance of gardens and outdoor spaces, including planting flowers, shrubs, and trees that are suitable for the local climate. Landscaping might also include hardscaping elements such as patios, walkways, and irrigation systems. Tree and Shrub Care: Trimming, pruning, and health assessments for trees and shrubs are important to prevent disease, encourage growth, and maintain safety. Irrigation Systems: Installation and maintenance of irrigation systems to ensure efficient water use, crucial in Albuquerque�s arid environment. This might include drip systems or smart irrigation technologies. Seasonal Cleanups: Removal of leaves, debris, and other waste, particularly during fall and spring, to maintain a neat appearance and prevent plant disease. Pest Control: Management of pests that can damage plants and lawns, using environmentally friendly methods where possible. Groundskeeping for Commercial Properties: Enhanced services that may include parking lot maintenance, exterior cleaning, and snow removal in winter months. Providers in Albuquerque may offer customized plans based on the unique requirements of the property and the preferences of the property owner. Additionally, they typically emphasize sustainable practices to cope with the region's water scarcity and environmental concerns.

title: NIH MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES
description: SOLICITATION NOTICE MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES Solicitation No. 75N99027R00002 The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Acquisition and Logistics Management (OALM), Construction, A&E, Facilities and Leasing Office (CAFLO), anticipates issuing a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a Multiple-Award Construction Contract (MACC) to support the ongoing construction, alteration, repair, and maintenance requirements of the NIH Office of Research Facilities (ORF). The resulting contracts will be multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) construction contracts. Work will be authorized through individually issued task orders. This acquisition is anticipated to be conducted using competitive negotiated procedures under FAR Part 15. The Government intends to award multiple IDIQ construction contracts under FAR Subpart 16.5. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis. The anticipated aggregate ceiling is $3 billion over an eight-year ordering period. Individual construction requirements will be competed through task orders among eligible MACC awardees in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the resulting contracts. The solicitation and resulting contracts will include procedures for adding and removing awardees during that period (on/off ramp). The initial seed-project scope estimated construction magnitude, applicable evaluation factors, and proposal submission requirements will be provided in the solicitation. SCOPE OF WORK Work under the MACC will primarily consist of general construction and may include, but is not limited to, maintenance, repair, painting, alterations, architectural work, mechanical systems, electrical systems, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), civil work, earthwork, fencing, structural work, steel fabrication and welding, roofing, building renovations, demolition, new building construction, sustainable construction, design-bid-build, and design-build projects. Individual task orders may include one or more construction disciplines and will vary in size, scope, and complexity. All work will be performed in accordance with the requirements, specifications, drawings, and other documents applicable to each individual task order. LOCATIONS OF WORK The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Research Facilities (ORF) is the steward of NIH facilities and is responsible for the planning, design, construction, acquisition, maintenance and operation of NIH owned facilities, which include campuses in: � Bethesda, Maryland, � Frederick, Maryland, � Poolesville, Maryland, � Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, � The Rocky Mountain Laboratories (RML) in Hamilton, Montana. NAICS CODE AND SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. PSC Code: Y1JZ The corresponding small business size standard is $45 million. The NAICS code and small business size standard applicable to the initial seed project is also anticipated to be NAICS 236220 and $45 million, respectively. ACQUISITION STRATEGY AND ANTICIPATED AWARDS This acquisition will be conducted using full and open competition with reserves for eligible small business concerns. NIH anticipates awarding up to twenty (20) IDIQ contracts, consisting of: Approximately four (4) unrestricted/full-and-open awards; and Approximately sixteen (16) awards under small business reserves. The small business reserves are anticipated to include eligible concerns in the following categories: Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Small Business; Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); and Participants in the SBA 8(a) Business Development Program. The solicitation will identify the anticipated distribution of the sixteen (16) reserve awards among the applicable small business and socioeconomic categories and will establish the eligibility requirements applicable to each reserve. NIH anticipates approximately four (4) awards in each socioeconomic reserve. Offerors must meet all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the category under which they submit an offer. BONDING CAPACITY Offerors competing for an unrestricted/full-and-open award shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $100 million for a single project; and $300 million aggregate bonding capacity. Offerors competing for an award under a small business reserve shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $3 million for a single project; and $10 million aggregate bonding capacity. The solicitation will establish the specific documentation required to demonstrate bonding capacity. Performance and payment bond requirements applicable to individual construction task orders will be established in accordance with the solicitation, resulting contracts, applicable law and regulation, and the requirements of each task order. SMALL BUSINESS ELIGIBILITY AND JOINT VENTURES Offerors seeking an award under a small business reserve must satisfy all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the applicable reserve category and NAICS code. The solicitation will identify any documentation required to establish an offeror's eligibility for the applicable small business or socioeconomic category. Small business concerns intending to submit an offer as a joint venture must comply with all applicable SBA joint venture requirements, including applicable requirements governing SBA-approved Mentor-Prot�g� relationships. Prospective offerors should consult current SBA regulations and guidance concerning joint ventures and the SBA Mentor-Prot�g� Program at www.sba.gov. CONTRACT CEILING AND ORDERING PERIOD The aggregate maximum value of all contracts and task orders awarded under the MACC will not exceed $3,000,000,000.00 over the entire ordering period. The $3 billion ceiling applies collectively to all MACC contracts and is not a per-contractor ceiling. The anticipated ordering period will consist of one eight-year ordering period. There is no anticipated annual or individual-contractor ceiling other than limitations established by the terms of the resulting contracts and individual task orders. MACC holders will remain eligible to compete for task orders, subject to the terms and conditions of their contracts, until expiration of the ordering period or exhaustion of the aggregate MACC ceiling, whichever occurs first. TASK ORDERS All work under the MACC will be authorized through individual task orders. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis and will be separately priced. Each task order will establish the applicable scope of work, specifications and drawings, period of performance, applicable wage determination, bonding requirements, and other project-specific requirements. Task orders may be competed among all eligible MACC holders or restricted to eligible small business MACC holders in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated maximum value of an individual task order is $800 million. Eligibility to compete for individual task orders may be subject to project-specific requirements, including required bonding capacity. GUARANTEED MINIMUM The Government's guaranteed minimum under each resulting IDIQ contract will be $1,000. The guaranteed minimum will be satisfied through issuance of a task order. The $1,000 guaranteed minimum is a contractual minimum obligation and should not be interpreted as establishing the minimum dollar value of all future task orders. title: NJ-NY ERFO FW WARI 2019-1(1) - Wallkill River National Wildlife Refuge
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for Wallkill River National Wildlife Refuge, Project NJ-NY ERFO FW WARI 2019-1(1), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000005, located in Sussex County, New Jersey; and Orange County, New York. The project consists of repairs to the Winding Waters Trail, Liberty Loop Trail (NE), Liberty Loop Trail (SW), and Dagmar Dale Nature Trail. The work includes embankment repairs, trail reconstruction, culvert replacement, stream regrading, headwall and wingwall installation, and other miscellaneous work. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. All visitors must sign in at the main entrance of the Quantum Park facility and wait to be escorted by a Government employee to Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD) in Suite 200. Visitors must then register with the EFLHD Receptionist. A Government employee will collect all bids. Prior to the bid opening, a Government employee will escort all bidders to the bid opening. Unescorted visitors will be denied entry and no exceptions will be made. Bidders are encouraged to submit bids electronically per the instructions provided in the solicitation.

title: MP-090088, EM AS Neuenhof - jonction de Dietikon revêtement / entrepreneur-construction
description: Le revêtement existant sur la N01, entre le pont de la Limmat à Neuenhof et la jonction de Dietikon, a atteint la fin de sa durée de vie. La remise en état de ce tronçon doit permettre d’atteindre une durée de vie de 15 ans sans entretien. Il est prévu de remplacer le revêtement, y compris environ 30 % de la couche de liaison. Parallèlement, les couvercles de regards en mauvais état situés sur la chaussée doivent être remplacés, des mesures EES doivent être mises en œuvre et des mesures concernant la signalisation et le marquage doivent être prises (remplacement des dispositifs de guidage, des plaquettes de repérage hectométriques et des panneaux de kilométrage. Remplacement partiel des panneaux de signalisation et nouveau marquage après les travaux de revêtement). Les travaux de revêtement s’effectueront, selon la phase de construction, de nuit avec réduction du nombre de voies ou fermeture de rampes d’accès, et en partie de jour avec l’intervention de l’ASTRA Bridge.

title: Netherlands – Banking services – Bancaire Dienstverlening
description: De aanbesteding moet leiden tot een overeenkomst met een bank die voldoende expertise heeft om de universiteit te faciliteren met betrekking tot het huidige en toekomstige betalingsverkeer. Aan u wordt gevraagd een offerte uit te brengen voor het volgende: 1. Verzorgen van het betalingsverkeer voor de Universiteit Leiden, waarvoor onder meer een systeem voor elektronisch bankieren ter beschikking wordt gesteld, waarin de bankrekeningen van de eenheden van de universiteit en de gelieerde stichtingen worden ondergebracht binnen één complex waarin ofwel een dagelijkse saldoregulatie ofwel op andere wijze een zero balance structuur mogelijk is en rentecompensatie kan plaatsvinden althans ten aanzien van universitaire rekeningen. 2. Een voorstel om de handlingskosten van de kasstromen binnen de universiteit zoveel mogelijk, op een gebruikersvriendelijke wijze, te verlagen door o.a. een vermindering van het aantal bankrekeningen en een optimalisatie van het overig betalingsverkeer (m.n. ontvangsten voor diverse diensten). 3. overige diensten die de bank kan leveren om de universiteit te ondersteunen in het bereiken van hieraan verwante doelstellingen en bij het behouden van een financiële stabiele positie. Daarbij dient de bank de universiteit te wijzen op eventuele geïdentificeerde risico's in de bedrijfsvoering. Essentieel is dat de bank is aangehaakt op de procedure met betrekking tot schatkistbankieren. Verder moet de bank internationaal (wereld) betalingsverkeer kunnen faciliteren. Daarnaast is het belangrijk dat de bank gedurende de overeenkomst in staat is (proactief) op nieuwe ontwikkelingen te reageren, deze actief aan de Universiteit Leiden voor te stellen en deze te implementeren.

title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: DC Recruiter
description: DC Recruiter: Broad-Spectrum Immune Enhancer from scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a differentiated approach to multi-pathogen infection prevention by using a self-assembling peptide nanofiber to recruit and activate dendritic cells (DCs), the immune system�s natural sentinels. Unlike pathogen-specific vaccines or therapeutics, it is designed to help trigger an early immune response regardless of the infecting agent. Its needle-free, spray-friendly concept adds practicality. The Challenge: DC Recruiter addresses a persistent and highly consequential gap in infection management: the need for a rapid, broadly effective way to stimulate immune defense before the specific pathogen is known. In many exposure scenarios, the body encounters a threat before clinicians can identify the cause, and that delay can reduce the effectiveness of conventional interventions. Current vaccines, antibiotics and antivirals are generally designed to act against a known target, which limits their usefulness when exposure is unexpected, diagnosis is delayed or the pathogen is unfamiliar. That limitation creates a clear unmet need for a fast-acting, broad-spectrum approach that can be deployed early, with minimal complexity, and in settings where rapid response matters most, including outbreak situations, field environments and other high-risk conditions. Problems Solved: DC Recruiter solves this problem by using a specific peptide selected to bind to dendritic cells. By leveraging a self-assembling peptide nanofiber platform, the technology is designed to help �wake up� immune surveillance early, before infection can progress unchecked. Rather than relying on a treatment matched to one virus or bacterium, it creates the potential for broad-spectrum immune support across many different infectious threats. Its ability to provide broad-spectrum immune support makes it especially compelling for situations where time is critical and conventional options may be too specific, too slow or too late to provide immediate protection. The needle-free, spray-friendly concept also adds practical value by supporting easier administration and broader accessibility, strengthening its fit for real-world use cases that demand rapid, flexible deployment. Key Advantages: Helps the body respond faster after exposure to an infection Works in a broad, pathogen-agnostic way rather than against just one germ Targets dendritic cells, which help alert and activate the immune system May be useful when the exact cause of infection is not yet known Could be helpful in outbreak, emergency, or high-risk settings Has the potential to be easier to use because it is designed as a needle-free spray Market Applications: Infectious Disease Prevention (early-response immune support, broad-spectrum protection) Outbreak Response and Public Health (rapid deployment, exposure mitigation) Defense and National Security (force protection, biological threat preparedness) Consumer Health and Wellness (easy-to-use immune support, potential spray format) Pharmaceuticals and Biotech (next-generation immunomodulation, platform development) Emergency Preparedness (first-response tools, high-risk exposure settings) Development Status: TRL 3 US Patent pending LA-UR-26-24915 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov.
